subject.title: fix(telegram): DM lane stays dead after a wedged handler keeps it guarded; escalate to a supervised gateway restart

question: Should `processRestartRequired` become a generic public channel snapshot contract that may trigger supervised whole-gateway replacement, or should this recovery request remain a narrow Telegram-owned seam?
rationale: Both designs can preserve the safety invariant, but repository policy cannot determine whether whole-process lifecycle control belongs in the stable cross-plugin status contract; that API and blast-radius choice requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Approve the generic contract
options.body: Keep the additive snapshot field, cross-channel policy, durable budget, and supervised-only routing, and explicitly document that trusted channel plugins may request bounded gateway replacement.

options.title: Use a Telegram-owned seam
options.body: Replace the public snapshot field with a narrow injected recovery request owned by Telegram while retaining the same wedge detection, durable budget, and supervised process handoff.

options.title: Pause automatic recovery
options.body: Do not merge process replacement until maintainers are comfortable granting channel runtime status this lifecycle effect, leaving manual gateway restart as the recovery path.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic contract
recommendation.body: Keep the additive snapshot field, cross-channel policy, durable budget, and supervised-only routing, and explicitly document that trusted channel plugins may request bounded gateway replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is repeated ownership of the Telegram spool, claim, and polling lifecycle that defines when the lane is truly unrecoverable in-process.
